subject: general
question: How is the character of Lady Catherine de Bourgh employed in the novel as a criticism of society?

options.text: She is purely comic relief and has no other significance.
She represents the struggle of the working class against the landed gentry.
She symbolizes ideal maternal love and wisdom.
She represents social tyranny and class prejudice.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Symbolism of Class Consciousness:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly mentions that personages like the "imperious Lady Catherine de Bourgh" symbolize the "hard and silly aspects of class consciousness."
 
 
 
• ***Satirical Role:***
 
 
• Austen uses characters like Lady Catherine to point out the "absurdities of the class structure" through the liberal use of irony and satire.
 
 
 
• ***Character Trait:***
 
 
• By describing her as "imperious," the text highlights her role as a figure of social tyranny, using her high status to dictate the lives of those she deems inferior.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **She represents social tyranny and class prejudice.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect. While her behavior may be absurd, the text states she has the significant role of symbolizing class structure.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect. Lady Catherine is part of the high-ranking nobility, not the working class.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect. The passage describes her as "imperious" rather than wise or maternally loving.
